messages.content: This is Sales Heatmap, a live sales overview widget for Uno Platform, fed by an MVUX feed.

Sales Heatmap is one Uno single project, `SalesHeatmap/SalesHeatmap.csproj` (Uno.Sdk from `global.json`, heads net10.0-android, net10.0-browserwasm and net10.0-desktop; UnoFeatures Material, Dsp, Hosting, Toolkit, Logging, MVUX, Navigation, SkiaRenderer).

Key files:
- `App.xaml.cs`: the host (logging, navigation) and the routes: `Shell` (with `ShellModel`) holds the region, and `Main` (`MainPage`, `MainModel`) is the default route. `Presentation/Shell.xaml` is the Toolkit's `ExtendedSplashScreen`.
- `App.xaml`: `MaterialToolkitTheme` with its `Colors` set to `<ut:ThemeColors OverrideSource="ms-appx:///Styles/ColorPaletteOverride.xaml" />` (generated from `ColorPaletteOverride.json` by the `Dsp` feature; the one place brand colours live, and what Studio's Themes tab edits), plus the only colour with no palette role, `PositiveColor` / `PositiveBrush` (a rise), in its Light and Default theme dictionaries.
- `Presentation/MainModel.cs`: `IFeed<SalesSnapshot> Snapshot`, built with `Feed.AsyncEnumerable`: the initial snapshot, then a new random one every two seconds on a `PeriodicTimer` that honours the feed's cancellation token.
- `Presentation/SalesSnapshot.cs`: an immutable record (monthly and yearly totals and changes; Los Angeles, New York and Canada with their changes), with `Initial` and `NextRandom(Random)`.
- `Presentation/MainPage.xaml`: a `FeedView` on `Snapshot` (a `ProgressRing` while it loads) whose value template puts the widget in a `Viewbox` (`StretchDirection="DownOnly"`, at most 400 wide), so the card lays out at 400 and scales down on a phone.
- `Presentation/SalesHeatmapWidget.xaml(.cs)`: the widget, a `UserControl` with one `Snapshot` dependency property. The XAML is the card (title and LIVE dot, the heatmap's host `Grid`, monthly and yearly figures, top regions). Its resources hold three brushes whose `Color` is bound with `{ThemeResource}` (`HeatCellBrush` = `PrimaryColor`, `RiseBrush` = `PositiveColor`, `FallBrush` = `ErrorColor`), so a theme or palette change recolours them in place. The code-behind builds 12 by 8 `Rectangle` cells on load, all filled with `HeatCellBrush`, and runs three `DispatcherTimer`s: every 150 ms a few cells get a new random target and every cell eases toward its target, changing its `Opacity` only when its step (of 32) changes; every 16 ms the figures ease 10% toward the snapshot and the timer stops once they are within 0.5; every 500 ms the LIVE dot blinks. Text is set only when it changes. A change shows a drawn triangle (`Path`, flipped for a fall; the Roboto font has no arrow glyph) and its text in `RiseBrush` or `FallBrush`. `Unloaded` stops and unhooks all three timers.

Theming: no colour, font size, corner radius or spacing literal anywhere. Text uses the Material type styles (`TitleMedium`, `HeadlineSmall`, `BodyMedium`, `LabelSmall`…), surfaces and text the role brushes (`SurfaceBrush`, `SurfaceVariantBrush`, `BackgroundBrush`, `OnSurfaceBrush`, `OnSurfaceVariantBrush`, `OutlineBrush`, `OutlineVariantBrush`, `PrimaryBrush`), spacing the `Space*` tokens and corners `Radius*CornerRadius`. Under Material on this Uno.Themes build `SpaceN00` is N x 8 px (Space300 = 24) and `RadiusN00` is N x 4 px. Keep it that way: to rebrand, edit the palette.

Traps: MVUX pages bind with `{Binding}`; inside the `FeedView` template the value is `Data`. The heatmap cells are decorative and random; the snapshot drives the figures only.

Data is simulated; nothing leaves the device. There are no tests.

Build: `dotnet build SalesHeatmap/SalesHeatmap.csproj -f net10.0-desktop`, or `-f net10.0-browserwasm` for WebAssembly.

The app is built and running. The user may ask me to modify it.
